issues.desc: CHK-001 creates evidence/artifact, evidence/admissibility, evidence/repro subdir entrypoints over existing implementation, but evidence/ already holds flat artifact-store.ts and types.ts. Checklist does not define how the new subdir entrypoints relate to those flat files (re-export vs duplicate vs move). Architecture doc requires single-source-of-truth, so PLAN should pin down the flat-to-subdir mapping.

priority=high looks like a mention-vs-modify keyword false positive: gate/gates appears only in negated/mention form and the story does not change gate or lifecycle behavior. If confirmed in PLAN, consider dismissing the high-risk signal rather than adding unnecessary decision overhead.

CHK-002 lists a lifecycle-control dashboard entrypoint, but the global-lifecycle-control-plane doc names dashboard as a projection concern. Confirm dashboard maps to an intended module so PLAN does not scaffold an unsanctioned path.

Standalone readability: background references the recommended source structure from the architecture review without naming the source document/section. relatedDocs recover this, but naming evidence-platform-architecture.md Storage module layout would aid fresh-context readability.

User-value coverage gap: trigger records the user asking to both develop the structure AND estimate milestones, but no checklist item produces or explicitly defers a milestone/roadmap estimate. After completion the user is still left wondering when the real migration happens and on what timeline. Add a milestone deliverable OR have background.md explicitly state milestone estimation is deferred to a follow-up.

No user/developer-observable acceptance per checklist item. CHK-001/002/003 describe engineering mechanics but none state the observable signal proving the item done, such as new imports resolving while legacy imports still compile. For a no-behavior-change refactor whose proof is build/import behavior, completion recognition is fuzzy without it.

Re-export compatibility shells risk reading as a finished migration. New layered dirs re-export still-flat implementations; a future host could mistake new paths for a completed move. Completion outcome should make explicit that these are temporary adapters and implementation has not fully moved yet.
